# Proto-personas, journeys and service blueprints

Proto-personas and assumed journeys. Written from the tools, the standard and the people this kind of service usually serves; not yet tested in research with real users (open item O-03).

NDL PubSec MCP is an independent prototype. It is not a government service and is not endorsed by any government department.

## Proto-personas

### Catalogue publisher

Publishes datasets for an organisation to data.gov.uk, often alongside another job.

- **Wants to:** Get records complete and correct before a return, an audit or a release, without learning the whole standard first.
- **What gets in the way:** Finds out which attributes are required only when something is rejected; Catalogue fields and xGov MEM attributes have different names; No quick way to see what a record still lacks
- **Tools:** `dataset_describe`, `metadata_validate`
- **Journey:** Fix a catalogue record
- **How they can shape it:** Tells us where a verdict disagrees with the standard or with how records are really kept. Shares the metadata readiness checklist with other publishers.

### Analyst or researcher

Answers questions with data and needs to know quickly what exists, who holds it and whether it can be reused.

- **Wants to:** Find candidate datasets, judge whether they are fit for the question, and cite them properly.
- **What gets in the way:** Keyword search returns many near-duplicates; Licence, update frequency and format are buried; Hard to tell a maintained dataset from an abandoned one
- **Tools:** `catalogue_search`, `dataset_describe`, `standard_explain`, `api_search`
- **Journey:** Find and judge data
- **How they can shape it:** Suggests searches that went badly so the tool descriptions and results can improve. Shares the prompt library with their analysis community.

### Metadata or standards lead

Looks after metadata quality across an organisation or a community of publishers.

- **Wants to:** See how far records are from xGov MEM, find the common gaps, and explain the standards in plain terms.
- **What gets in the way:** Conformance is checked by hand, one record at a time; Colleagues ask what a standard is for and where it stands; Business terms are drafted in many places with no record of review
- **Tools:** `metadata_validate`, `standard_explain`, `term_lookup`, `api_search`
- **Journey:** Assess a set of records
- **How they can shape it:** Checks validation against their own records and reports disagreements with the model. Runs the show-and-tell and the co-design session in their community.

### Developer or AI builder

Connects tools to assistants, agents or pipelines and has to answer for what they do.

- **Wants to:** Add data discovery and metadata checks to an assistant safely, with predictable inputs and no side effects.
- **What gets in the way:** Needs to know exactly what each tool reads and returns; Must show that nothing writes, sends or stores data; Wants to try tools before wiring them in
- **Tools:** `catalogue_search`, `dataset_describe`, `metadata_validate`, `standard_explain`, `term_lookup`, `domain_list`, `api_search`, `server_search`
- **Journey:** Set up and try
- **How they can shape it:** Opens pull requests with tests, and reports defects with a way to reproduce them. Shows other builders how the server is checked: the defect register and its checks.

### Policy or product colleague

Not a data specialist. Uses an AI assistant to understand what data exists and what the standards mean.

- **Wants to:** Get a plain-English answer they can trust, with a link to the source they can pass on.
- **What gets in the way:** Jargon: DCAT, CURIE, crosswalk; Cannot tell whether an assistant's answer came from a real source; Does not know who to ask
- **Tools:** `catalogue_search`, `standard_explain`, `term_lookup`, `api_search`
- **Journey:** Find and judge data
- **How they can shape it:** Tells us where an answer was unclear, so explanations and the glossary improve. Points colleagues at the glossary and the worked examples.

### Data champion

Promotes good data practice inside their organisation, usually on top of a day job.

- **Wants to:** Show colleagues something useful in under an hour and leave them able to carry on alone.
- **What gets in the way:** Little time to prepare material; Needs examples that work on the day; Hard to collect feedback in a form others can act on
- **Tools:** `metadata_validate`, `catalogue_search`, `standard_explain`
- **Journey:** Champion and contribute
- **How they can shape it:** Collects feedback from sessions and raises it through the contact form. Uses the champion pack and the session plan from the toolkit.

### Contributor or co-designer

Wants to shape the service: report, test, suggest, design or code.

- **Wants to:** Make a change that is accepted, and see what happened to their idea.
- **What gets in the way:** Unclear where ideas go and how they are decided; Worried a change will be rejected on process; No visible roadmap
- **Tools:** `standard_explain`, `domain_list`
- **Journey:** Champion and contribute
- **How they can shape it:** Joins co-design sessions, improves the standards list, writes tests and checks. Brings a second organisation's view, so the work is not shaped by one.

## Journeys and service blueprints

### Set up and try

For: Developer or AI builder.

| Lane | Discover | Try without installing | Install | Connect | First call | Keep using |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| What the person does | Lands on this page from a link or a search | Pastes a record into the checker | Clones, installs and builds | Adds the server to an assistant's settings | Asks a question that needs a tool | Updates to new releases |
| What they see (front stage) | What it does, what it is not, the tools | A verdict with each finding and its path | Four commands | A configuration snippet for each assistant | An answer that names its source | What has changed, newest first |
| What happens behind the scenes (back stage) | Static page generated from the repository | The server's own validator, compiled into the page | npm ci and the TypeScript build | The assistant starts the server over stdio | One read-only tool call | Release notes generated from the changelog |
| What supports it | GitHub Pages; the build in CI | xGov MEM model at a pinned commit | Node.js 20 or later | MCP client in the assistant | data.gov.uk catalogue API | GitHub releases; weekly live smoke test |
| Likely pain point | Is this safe to use? | My record is in another shape | Node version or path mistakes | The tools do not appear | Not sure which tool was used | Breaking changes |
| What this portal offers | Read-only statement, defect register, open register | Example records and the record template | Troubleshooting in the user guide | Inspector route to test the server on its own | Worked examples show the call behind each prompt | Changelog and versioned releases |
| Assumed effort (1 easy to 5 hard, modelled) | 2 | 1 | 3 | 3 | 2 | 2 |

### Find and judge data

For: Analyst or researcher, Policy or product colleague.

| Lane | Ask | Search | Shortlist | Describe | Judge | Use and cite |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| What the person does | Describes what they need in their own words | Narrows by publisher or topic | Picks two or three candidates | Opens one dataset in detail | Decides whether it is fit for the question | Uses the data and cites the catalogue entry |
| What they see (front stage) | The assistant's reply | Titles, publishers, licences, formats, dates and links | Comparable facts side by side | Description, distributions and a draft xGov MEM record | Update frequency, licence, standards it follows | A link to the source |
| What happens behind the scenes (back stage) | The assistant chooses catalogue_search | catalogue_search calls package_search | Results stay as returned; nothing is ranked by guesswork | dataset_describe calls package_show and the crosswalk | standard_explain gives each standard's purpose and status | Links come straight from the catalogue |
| What supports it | Tool descriptions written for assistants | data.gov.uk | Catalogue metadata as published | The crosswalk, tested against live records | Standards list with provenance labels | data.gov.uk dataset pages |
| Likely pain point | Too vague a question | Near-duplicates | Missing licence or dates | Gaps in the source record | Unsure what a standard means | Citing an assistant instead of the source |
| What this portal offers | Prompt library with good starting questions | Tip: ask for a table with last-updated dates to spot stale entries | dataset_describe reports what is missing | Gaps are named, never filled in by guess | Plain-English explanations and the glossary | Tip: always cite the catalogue link |
| Assumed effort (1 easy to 5 hard, modelled) | 1 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 3 | 1 |

### Fix a catalogue record

For: Catalogue publisher.

| Lane | Pick a record | See the gaps | Fill the gaps | Check | Publish | Re-check |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| What the person does | Chooses a record due for a return or review | Asks for the record against xGov MEM | Finds the missing facts from the people who hold them | Validates the corrected record | Updates the record in their own catalogue | Checks again after the catalogue harvests |
| What they see (front stage) | The record in their catalogue | A draft record and a list of what it lacks | The record template | Errors to fix and warnings to consider, with paths | Their catalogue's own screens | Fewer or no gaps |
| What happens behind the scenes (back stage) | Nothing yet | dataset_describe and the crosswalk | Nothing is guessed on their behalf | metadata_validate or the in-page checker | This server never writes anywhere | dataset_describe against the updated entry |
| What supports it | Their own publishing process | Live catalogue; pinned model | Their data owners | Validator agreed with the model's own tests | Their publishing route | Catalogue harvest cycle |
| Likely pain point | Which record first? | Long list of gaps | Facts held by someone else | Misspelt names, values outside the list | Two systems to keep in step | Harvest delay |
| What this portal offers | Readiness checklist to prioritise | Gaps grouped as required or recommended | Checklist explains each attribute in plain terms | Worked examples for the common mistakes | Tip: keep the validated JSON with the change | Re-check step in the tutorial |
| Assumed effort (1 easy to 5 hard, modelled) | 1 | 2 | 4 | 2 | 3 | 1 |

### Assess a set of records

For: Metadata or standards lead.

| Lane | Sample | Check each record | Find patterns | Explain | Report | Re-check |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| What the person does | Chooses a publisher or a theme to look at | Asks the assistant to describe and check each in turn | Looks for the attributes missing most often | Explains the gaps and standards to publishers | Writes up findings and actions | Repeats the sample after fixes |
| What they see (front stage) | Search results for that slice | One verdict per record | A summary table | Plain-English explanations | Their own report | Change over time |
| What happens behind the scenes (back stage) | catalogue_search with an organisation filter | One read-only call per record; findings capped at 100 per call | The assistant tallies tool results | standard_explain and term_lookup | Nothing is stored by this server | Same calls, same pinned model |
| What supports it | data.gov.uk | Validator and crosswalk | The 50-record sample on this page as a baseline | Standards list and glossary | Their governance route | Versioned releases |
| Likely pain point | Large result sets | Assistant stops part way through a long list | Assistant arithmetic can be wrong | Terms used differently across teams | Evidence hard to reproduce | Model changes between checks |
| What this portal offers | Tip: page through with limit and offset | Prompt that asks for a table and a running count | Tip: ask for the per-record table, then check the totals | term_lookup shows who drafted a term and its review level | Record the model commit and date with the findings | Model commit is shown on every result |
| Assumed effort (1 easy to 5 hard, modelled) | 2 | 3 | 3 | 2 | 3 | 2 |

### Champion and contribute

For: Data champion, Contributor or co-designer.

| Lane | Try | Show others | Gather feedback | Raise it | Co-design | Contribute |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| What the person does | Uses the checker and a few prompts | Runs a short session for colleagues | Collects what worked and what did not | Sends feedback, a bug or an idea | Joins a session to shape a change | Opens a pull request |
| What they see (front stage) | Worked examples that work on the day | Session plan and champion pack | Feedback questions in the session plan | A short GitHub form | Personas and journeys to react to | Contributing guide and checks |
| What happens behind the scenes (back stage) | Examples checked by the validator at build time | Toolkit files generated with the page | Nothing collected by this site | An issue, labelled and triaged | Decisions recorded as ADRs | CI, code scanning and the repository gate |
| What supports it | This page | Toolkit | Their own notes | Issue templates | Open register and roadmap | Maintainer review |
| Likely pain point | Demo fails live | Little time to prepare | Feedback lost after the session | Not sure which form | Ideas disappear | Process feels heavy |
| What this portal offers | In-browser checker needs no install or network | A 45-minute plan, ready to use | Feedback questions mirror the contact form | Get involved section maps each need to a form | Open register shows what happened to each item | Tutorial for a first, small change |
| Assumed effort (1 easy to 5 hard, modelled) | 1 | 3 | 2 | 1 | 3 | 4 |

## Questions to test in research

- Do these roles match the people who actually use the catalogue and the model? Which are missing?
- At which stage does each journey really break down?
- Which of the portal's offers are used, and which are ignored?
